What is CAN number?

CAN is the Citizen Access Number — the unique identity number a citizen is issued and quotes on an application. Its length names the counter that issued it: 15 digits (133 series) from a CSC counter, 12 digits from the TN citizen portal. It does not by itself tell you the submission channel.

What is Sub-Registrar?

SRO is the Sub-Registrar Office, where a sale deed is registered. When a deed is registered there, its IGRS system raises the patta mutation off the registered document and issues an IGRS Form 6 number. What is CSC?

There is no IGRS Form 6 number, because no registered deed raised it.

What is Sub-Registrar?

SRO is the Sub-Registrar Office, where a sale deed is registered. What is CSC?

What is a CAN number, and does its length tell me the submission channel?

CAN is the Citizen Access Number, the unique identity number a citizen quotes on an application; every application carries one. Its length names the counter that ISSUED it, not the channel the application came in through - 15 digits (133 series) from a CSC counter, 12 digits from the TN citizen portal. A Sub-Registrar referral carries a 12-digit portal-issued CAN even though no citizen keyed it in, so a 12-digit CAN does not mean "citizen" and a 15-digit CAN does not mean "CSC". The channel is decided by the source name and camp flag on the file.

What is a field visit?

A field visit (field inspection or site inspection) is the on-site verification an SIS officer carries out at the actual land parcel. The officer visits the survey number in person, measures the boundaries and area, checks the boundary stones, looks for encroachment, collects the signatures of the applicant and all joint owners, and prepares field notes with photographs. It is mandatory for ISD (0154) and MERGE (0155) applications, must be scheduled within 15 working days of submission, and its date can only be changed with the Tahsildar's approval. NISD (0153) applications are verified from documents and normally need no field visit.

What is a temporary subdivision number?

A temporary subdivision number is a provisional number assigned by the Deputy Inspector Surveyor (DIS) to each proposed parcel in an ISD (0154) or MERGE (0155) application. It follows the format {existing_subdivision}/T{sequence}, for example 3/T1, 3/T2, 0/T1, 2A/T3. The Deputy Inspector Surveyor (DIS) assigns temporary subdivision numbers during the ISD workflow, after the Senior Draughtsman (SD) has prepared the survey sketch. What does the temporary number format mean?

The format is {existing_subdivision}/T{sequence}. The part before /T is the existing subdivision being split (0 if the survey has no prior subdivision). T stands for Temporary. The number after T is a sequence counter. For example, 3/T1 means "first temporary parcel from existing subdivision 3", and 0/T2 means "second temporary parcel from a survey with no prior subdivision".
